subject: Re: Request — custom erase slots & order-form language for data classes
messages:
From: Kelly Ramos <kelly.ramos@emeraldhealth.io>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Chong <mike.chong@emeraldhealth.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Custom erase windows — need order-form language and timelines

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. As we discussed in the intro call, Emerald Health needs bespoke retention and deletion commitments broken down by data class. High level ask:

- Persistent PHI-derived embeddings and audit logs: customer-managed retention windows (30/90/365 days options), with verifiable deletion certificates.
- Transient inference context (session metadata): immediate TTL-based eviction but we need formal SLA for the deletion request turnaround.
- Backups / snapshots: we want a maximum certified purge of 45 days after contract termination.

Two specific asks for the order form: 1) explicit deletion timelines per class, 2) language allowing an accelerated deletion option (14-day certified purge) for a fee. Can you send proposed order-form bullets and any limitations (e.g., backup snapshots, forensic hold exceptions)?

Attached is Emerald's template for SLA items (just a reference). Looking to finalize before legal review next month.

Cheers,
Kelly
Kelly Ramos
Head of InfoSec Programs
Emerald Health

Attachments: Emerald_SLA_ask_v1.pdf
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kelly Ramos <kelly.ramos@emeraldhealth.io>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Custom erase windows — need order-form language and timelines

Kelly — thanks for the clear summary. We can accommodate per-class windows; a few quick notes up front:

- We support TTL eviction for session context and can surface deletion confirmations via API.
- Persistent embeddings + logs: we can offer 30/90/365-day options in the order form. Backups and snapshots require a separate commitment: certified purge for backups is 45–90 days depending on the backup cadence and storage tier.
- Accelerated purge (14-day certified) is feasible as an add-on with a one-time remediation fee and a signed addendum (covers additional operational runbook and audit).

I want to confirm technical details with infra — looping in Rishi and Karthik to validate the snapshot timelines and whether we can guarantee the 14-day accelerated slot from the hosted environment. Will follow up with an order-form draft and proposed clause language.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Contracts
Redwood Inference

CC: rishi_malhotra, karthik_iyer
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Emerald — order-form retention question (internal)

Folks — forwarding Emerald's asks. Key clarifications we need:

1) For hosted customers (standard multi-tenant): what is realistic certified purge timeline for backups/snapshots after a deletion request or contract termination? Emerald expects 45 days as a cap for snapshots.
2) For persistent embeddings, can we add per-dataset retention windows that are enforced at the platform layer (not just recommended TTL)? If not, what's gap and how do we document it?
3) Confirm whether accelerated purge (14-day) requires a stop-the-world maintenance window or whether we can execute rolling deletion without >3h downtime.

I attached a draft custody matrix that we can adapt into the order form. Please reply with line-item language I can share with Kelly.

Attachments: custody_matrix.xlsx

-Marissa
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Emerald — order-form retention question (internal)

Marissa — technical notes below. High level: we can meet Emerald's asks with explicit order-form constraints and an optional accelerated purge addendum. Details: 

- Hosted backups/snapshots: standard retention for cold snapshots is up to 90 days. Certified purge of snapshots (including object-storage reclaim and metadata purge from index services) is possible within 45 days if Emerald opts into odd-hour maintenance windows and pays the remediation fee. Without the add-on, default snapshot purge is 90 days post-termination.

- Persistent embeddings & logs: we can institute per-dataset retention policies. Implementation will mark dataset IDs and enforce purge on the primary store; however, a separate reconciliation job for asynchronously cleaning caches and KV mirrors may take up to an additional 7 calendar days. We'll include the expected window in the SLA (e.g., primary purge within N days, final reconciliation within N+7 days).

- Accelerated 14-day option: doable but requires: emergency runbook, reserved ops slots, and a signed acknowledgment that some forensic traces (e.g., hardware-level snapshots or third-party backup replicas) may need contractual handback and third-party certs. This is operationally heavy and priced as a one-time $X,XXX fee + monthly reservation.

- Forensic hold: holds will supersede deletion requests and require coordination; we propose a clause that clarifies hold timelines and re-enablement.

I'll draft line language for the order form. Karthik — please add any legal/infra risk language around cross-region replica deletion and key management rotation implications.

-Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kelly Ramos <kelly.ramos@emeraldhealth.io>, Mike Chong <mike.chong@emeraldhealth.io>

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed order-form bullets & certified purge timelines (Emerald Health)

Hi Kelly / Mike — apologies for the turnaround; below is our proposed order-form language and the explicit timelines we can commit to. Attach: draft SLA + order form.

Summary table (to be copy/pasted into the order form):

- Data class: Session context (ephemeral) — Deletion SLA: API-triggered TTL; confirmation token within 24 hours; final system reconciliation within 72 hours.
- Data class: Derived embeddings (PHI-tagged) — Retention options: 30 / 90 / 365 days (customer to select). Primary store purge within 7 days of retention expiry or deletion request; final reconciliation and cache/KV clean within 14 additional days.
- Data class: Audit logs — Retention options: 90 / 365 days; certified deletion window for logs: primary purge within 30 days, backup snapshot purge within 45–90 days depending on backup cadence (45 days if Emerald opts into accelerated snapshot purge add-on).
- Data class: Backups / Snapshots — Standard certified purge: 90 days post-termination; Accelerated certified purge add-on: 45 days (requires addendum & remediation fee); Emergency accelerated purge (14 days) available as one-time engagement with reserved ops + third-party certs.

Forensic Hold: any active legal or regulator hold will suspend deletion obligations until hold release; Redwood will provide hold notifications and an estimated resume date.

Order-form clause (suggested text):
"Redwood will adhere to the data retention windows selected by Customer per Data Class. Upon Customer-initiated deletion or contract termination, Redwood will execute primary-store deletion within the times stated for each Data Class and will subsequently execute asynchronous reconciliation tasks to complete deletion from caches, mirrors, and backup systems within the stated reconciliation windows. Backup/snapshot deletion timelines depend on backup cadence and selected add-ons; accelerated options are available per the Addendum."

Attachments: Emerald_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf (draft order-form with table), custody_matrix.xlsx (mapping of dataset IDs to classes), orderform_lineitems_emerald.docx (pricing table & add-on terms)

Next steps: if this aligns with Emerald's expectations, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet (link included) and the accelerated-purge addendum if you want the 45-day snapshot commitment. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the table.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Contracts
Redwood Inference
